title: Yuezhi
capsule: The Yuezhi were a loosely confederated nomadic people attested in Chinese sources from at least the 3rd century BC, occupying the Gansu corridor and the Tarim Basin before being expelled westward by the Xiongnu under Modu Chanyu around 177–176 BC. After defeating the Saka (Scythians) in Sogdia and Bactria, the Great Yuezhi settled north of the Oxus, and by the mid-1st century BC the Kushana clan consolidated power over the other four Yuezhi clans, founding what would become the Kushan Empire under Kujula Kadphises around 30 CE. The Yuezhi as a distinct political entity dissolved into the Kushan polity by the early 1st century AD; a remnant called the Little Yuezhi reportedly survived in Qiang-adjacent territories in northwestern China.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is highly conjectural; Chinese chronicle accounts (Shiji, Hanshu) provide the migration narrative but no boundary data, and steppe ranges are reconstructed from archaeological cultures and coin distributions. The dataset's westward extent through Bactria is reasoned inference rather than documented territory.

rulers.name: Kujula Kadphises (Qiujiuque, Kushan yabghu who unified the Yuezhi)
